Specific objective/Outcome 2: Increased availability of mechanical and biomass supply services and access to finance for agri-MSEs to deploy CBGT consistently.  Specific objective/Outcome 3: ¿Buy-in¿ and support from relevant government agencies for further adoption and replication of CBGT in agri-food processing and other industries. Understanding that the enterprises will only deploy CBGT by having a strong business case for its adoption as well as a good quality, low-cost and conveniently accessible support service system, Oxfam and local partners will conduct comprehensive interventions to promote CBGT to MSEs and to develop local support service systems.

SHORT_DESCRIPTION: VIETNAMESE-FARM-CLEAN-MICROGRID
PROJECT_TITLE: VIETNAMESE-FARM-CLEAN-MICROGRID
LONG_DESCRIPTION: The project named as CLEANGRID (VIETNAMESE-FARM-CLEAN-MICROGRID) studies feasibility of a microgrid system with clean-renewable energy sources including PV, treated biogas generator, and secondary life battery as energy storage for Vietnamese agriculture (pig) farm.The project target is to provide an affordable, reliable, and clean energy solution to Vietnamese agriculture farm whilst mitigate the environmental pollution from farm waste and unreliable-off-grid power supply with good return of investment.The beneficiaries of the project are both the farm workforces-owner and the neighbor community where often locates in poor rural-remote-distant area with unreliable-off-grid power supply. With low-cost and mobile energy for basic appliances such as lighting, cooking, water-pump, communication, internet access, the project will address both gender and social inclusion as well as encourage equality.Livestock sector plays an important role in Vietnamese agriculture with 73% meat production is pork (26.7milion pig-head for 2014) and 70% pig-head (60% pork product) are from smallholder-householder farms (WB report). To mitigate this environmental issue from animal waste, waste process via anaerobic digestion for biogas generation and then using on cooking and power generation is often considered. Therefore, an affordable purification biogas process to improve the in-site cooking and power generation efficiency as well as reducing erosion issue on appliances is one major part of the project. The treatment is based on waste material (bentonite) from Vietnamese local mining and therefore, a cost-effective approach. The cooking via biogas could change the wood cooking behavior in the distant area leading to reduction of pollution-deforestation.As a tropical country, Vietnam has high-potential on solar power. However, for any microgrid system, energy storage is highly expensive. For cost-effective, energy storage system using secondary life battery from electric bike-vehicle in Vietnamese market is another topic of interests of the project. Also, a microgrid control system for maximizing energy conversion efficiency and minimizing energy consumption is essential.The battery and DC-AC inverter modules are designed and developed in such a way that it is detachable as a mobile module for distant-remote area where electricity system is unavailable for community service such as water-pump.To facilitate the scale-up of the microgrid system concept with different power levels and more renewable energy power integration such as biomass power generation, wind-turbine..., an energy conversion loss model for microgrid system is developed and validated via in-lab test. Also, a business model including investment cost, performance cost, return on investment, and potential CO2 capture-reduction is developed.

SHORT_DESCRIPTION: GREEN YOUTH LABS: TRAINING PROGRAM FOR INNOVATION AND A SOCIALLY EQUITABLE ENERGY TRANSITION (GREENYOU)
PROJECT_TITLE: Green Youth labs: Training program for innovation and a socially equitable energy transition (GreenYOU)
LONG_DESCRIPTION: The project aims to engage young people in low-carbon production and climate-friendly energy use at local and national levels. This is done through a two-stage training programme: an introductory module in North, Central and South Viet Nam (with 50 participants each) and an advanced module in Central Viet Nam, whose participants (30 in total) are selected based on pre-submitted project ideas. The training content is geared towards the needs of the participants to further develop their project ideas and includes a critical analysis and discussion of the overall socio-political framework. This is followed by a public innovation challenge in which young people (up to 35) submit proposals for pilot projects in various categories (e.g. technology, awareness-raising). Each year, the best 10 project ideas are selected by a panel of experts and the young people are supported conceptually and financially in their implementation through mentoring. The innovation challenge is coupled with an Energy Transition Fair, where the project proposals are presented to the private sector. In the third year, a Young Energy Summit takes place. With the support of experts, the alumni of the programme reflect on existing political frameworks and translate their own experiences into political recommendations, which are published in a position paper and presented to government and business representatives at the summit. The participation of climate activists from Germany and alumni from other FES young leadership programmes promotes a North-South exchange. The participants of the 10 best projects will go on a study trip to Germany to learn about the experiences made there with the energy transition. If the envisioned travels are not possible due to the Corona-Pandemic, a close virtual exchange is strived for.

SHORT_DESCRIPTION: SHIFT - SHIFTING INVESTMENT FLOWS TOWARDS GREEN TRANSFORMATION
PROJECT_TITLE: SHIFT - Shifting Investment Flows Towards Green Transformation
LONG_DESCRIPTION: The overall outcome of SHIFT is that green policy and investment frameworks for enhanced climate action in Viet Nam, especially in the energy sector, are improved (outcome). This helps Viet Nam on the path to (a) achieve its current conditional NDC target of reducing emissions by 27% in 2030 compared to BAU and its COP26 pledge to achieve net zero emissions by 2050, (b) to increase ambition of future NDC and (c) to achieve the SDGs and the objectives of the National Green Growth Strategy (impact). To this end, the project plans to deliver five interconnected outputs with associated work packages: (1) Improving the policy framework for green public and private investment and (2) improving the policy framework in favor of the energy transition, (3) increasing capacities of local financial players to supply green financial products, (4) increasing green investments by SMEs and other private sector actors, (5) facilitating a public discourse for an inclusive transition to a green economy.

SHORT_DESCRIPTION: SMALL AND MEDIUM-SIZED ENTERPRISES PROMOTE RESILIENCE, INCLUSION AND INNOVATIVE TRANSFORMATION/PETITES ET MOYENNES ENTREPRISES FAVORISENT LA RÉSILIENC
PROJECT_TITLE: Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises Promote Resilience, Inclusion and Innovative Transformation/Petites et moyennes entreprises favorisent la résilience, l'inclusion et la transformation novatrice
LONG_DESCRIPTION: This project seeks to enhance the socioeconomic wellbeing of ethnic minority women-focused small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) through clean growth in the agriculture sector of Yen Bai province of Vietnam. Project activities include: (1) providing technical assistance and training in inclusive business and financial management to ethnic minority women-focused micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs), cooperatives and producer groups, (2) piloting of renewable energy and energy efficiency technology solutions, and (3) raising awareness campaigns and training to improve the ability of ethnic minority women to be active participants and leaders in clean economic growth in agriculture and to reduce barriers to their economic participation and leadership. This project aims to benefit 20,000 ethnic minority women directly, target approximately 75 MSMEs in Yen Bai province and indirectly benefit 843,000 people. Rural areas, like Yen Bai, are highly vulnerable to the impacts of climate change, given low-lying roads and a high dependence on rain-fed agriculture. / Ce projet vise à améliorer le bien-être socioéconomique des petites et moyennes entreprises (PME), en mettant l'accent sur les femmes appartenant à des minorités ethniques, grâce à la croissance propre du secteur agricole de la province de Yen Bai au Vietnam. Les activités de ce projet comprennent : 1) fournir une assistance technique et une formation en gestion commerciale et financière inclusive aux microentreprises et aux petites et moyennes entreprises (MPME), aux coopératives et aux groupes de producteurs, en mettant l'accent sur les femmes appartenant à des minorités ethniques, 2) piloter des solutions technologiques en matière d'énergie renouvelable et d'efficacité énergétique, 3) lancer des campagnes de sensibilisation et d'activités de formation visant à améliorer la capacité des femmes appartenant à des minorités ethniques à participer activement à une croissance économique propre dans l'agriculture et à réduire les obstacles à leur participation économique et à leur leadership. Ce projet vise à bénéficier directement à 20 000 femmes issues de minorités ethniques, à cibler environ 75 MPME dans la province de Yen Bai et à bénéficier indirectement à 843 000 personnes. Les zones rurales, comme Yen Bai, sont très vulnérables aux effets des changements climatiques, en raison des routes dans les basses terres et de la forte dépendance à l'égard de l'agriculture pluviale.

SHORT_DESCRIPTION: INNOVATIVE & CLIMATE FINANCE MONITORING/CONTRAT DE SUIVI  IAIP
PROJECT_TITLE: Innovative & Climate Finance Monitoring/Contrat de suivi  IAIP
LONG_DESCRIPTION: The project will monitor and assess Global Affairs Canada's innovative finance and climate finance program portfolio progress against the program performance measurement framework and monitor and assess risks and performance of individual projects for blended finance outcomes including development finance, additional commercial finance mobilized (including financial returns), and the results achieved on development objectives. / Le projet surveillera et évaluera les progrès du portefeuille du Programme d'aide internationale à l'innovation (IAIP) par rapport au cadre de mesure de la performance du programme et surveillera et évaluera les risques et la performance des projets individuels pour les résultats du financement mixte, y compris le financement du développement, le financement commercial supplémentaire mobilisé (y compris rendements financiers), et les résultats obtenus sur les objectifs de développement.

SHORT_DESCRIPTION: SUPPORTING MEKONG ARCHITECTURE - MRC
PROJECT_TITLE: Supporting Mekong Architecture - MRC
LONG_DESCRIPTION: This investment has two activities both supporting Mekong River Commission 1) Australia's contribution to MRC's basket fund to implement its USD60 million five-year strategic plan 2021-2025 and 2) eWater's technical support to MRC. The key expected outcome of this investment is enhanced rules-based and transparent transboundary cooperation in the Mekong subregion. The investment will support stability of the subregion by seeking to protect established regional governance norms and strengthen regional architecture for building longer-term resilience. The investment is intended to continue through new activity covering the next MRC SP 2026-30.

SHORT_DESCRIPTION: AUSTRALIA-VIETNAM ENERGY TRANSITION PLATFORM (AVETP)
PROJECT_TITLE: Australia-Vietnam Energy Transition Platform (AVETP)
LONG_DESCRIPTION: The Australia-Vietnam Energy Transition Platform will have three strands. It will:- Establish the Renewable Energy Access Fund to facilitate an increase in the amount of investment by PIDG in Vietnam. This increased investment by PIDG will mobilise climate finance, accelerate energy transition and enable a higher number of people to access renewable energy sources. Avoided GHG emissions, and improved climate resilience of Vietnam's energy investments will be measured through a country outcome framework aligned with PIDG forthcoming 2023-2030 strategy.- Establish the Capital Markets for Climate Action Fund to allow PIDG company GuarantCo to push the frontier of Vietnam's capital market development for climate finance and energy transition, including bringing a focus on nature-based solutions.- Provide additional investment capital for InfraCo Asia and GuarantCo to invest in new deals in Vietnam.

SHORT_DESCRIPTION: PARTNERSHIPS FOR INFRASTRUCTURE (P4I)
PROJECT_TITLE: Partnerships for Infrastructure (P4I)
LONG_DESCRIPTION: P4I's goal is to contribute to 'quality infrastructure development that drives inclusive growth in Southeast Asia'. The end-of-investment outcome is 'Improved decision-making towards quality infrastructure underpinned by strong government-to-government partnerships'. P4I has three focus areas: planning and prioritisation of projects, implementation support for public infrastructure procurement, and sector policy and regulation. Climate change, gender equality and social inclusion are integrated throughout. P4I is delivered via four linked approaches: a quick response mechanism with high calibre advisers to provide advice at short notice to Southeast Asian governments and regional institutions, long term engagement through government-to-government partnerships, technical assistance that supplements and supports government to government partnerships, and regional networking and learning to bring together Australian experts with Southeast Asian counterparts.

SHORT_DESCRIPTION: AUS4GROWTH (VIETNAM)
PROJECT_TITLE: Aus4Growth (Vietnam)
LONG_DESCRIPTION: The Australia-Vietnam Partnership for Economic Growth will extend Australia's longstanding partnership with Vietnam to support Vietnam 's ambitions of becoming an upper middle-income country by 2030 and a high-income country by 2045. The partnership  will support key reforms in sectors that are fundamental drivers of sustained and inclusive economic growth, including transport infrastructure, energy, and trade, while also strengthening the overall competitiveness of the economy. It will  build Vietnam's capacity to engage in, and support the international rules-based trading system and will contribute to expanding the trade and investment relationship between Australia and Vietnam.The Partnership will help guide and coordinate the activities of other Australian-funded multilateral and regional economic programs to ensure we maximize our combined resources and adopt a joined up a approach to Australia's economic development assistance in Vietnam.

SHORT_DESCRIPTION: AUSTRALIA - MEKONG WATER FACILITY
PROJECT_TITLE: Australia - Mekong Water Facility
LONG_DESCRIPTION: The need for effective and rules-based water governance in the Greater Mekong region has never been so apparent.  Economic growth, future quality of life and regional stability are strongly linked to the choices made by countries on how to share, develop and manage water to produce food and energy, maintain vital ecosystems and sustain livelihoods. Australia provides $14.86 million grant to Australian Water Partnership to manage Australia-Mekong Water Facility (2019-2024). Through this Facility it will provide government to government line of cooperation, it will offer a responsive, nimble and flexible mechanism for Australia to further enhance our existing water-related partnerships with the governments of the region. The overall goal of the Facility is to enhance rules-based governance for water, food and energy security in the Greater Mekong region.

The end-of-investment outcome is 'Improved decision-making towards quality infrastructure underpinned by strong government-to-government partnerships'. P4I has three focus areas: planning and prioritisation of projects, implementation support for public infrastructure procurement, and sector policy and regulation. Climate change, gender equality and social inclusion are integrated throughout. P4I is delivered via four linked approaches: a quick response mechanism with high calibre advisers to provide advice at short notice to Southeast Asian governments and regional institutions, long term engagement through government-to-government partnerships, technical assistance that supplements and supports government to government partnerships, and regional networking and learning to bring together Australian experts with Southeast Asian counterparts.

SHORT_DESCRIPTION: INCLUSIVE WATER GOVERNANCE AND STRENGTHENING CLIMATE RESILIENCE IN THE MEKONG REGION
PROJECT_TITLE: Inclusive Water Governance and Strengthening Climate Resilience in the Mekong Region
LONG_DESCRIPTION: Building on Oxfam's Inclusion Project, this investment has two complementary activities supporting CSOs, community and women leaders to participate in water governance decision-making and strengthen community climate resilience in the Mekong sub-region. It supports CSO partners, women leaders and communities in Cambodia, Laos, Myanmar, Thailand and Vietnam and at the regional level, to engage with and influence governments, inter-governmental bodies and the private sector in water resource governance, planning and development. It also supports targeted community and local authorities in the region to strengthen their disaster risk management and climate change adaptation through better access and use of hydro-meteorological data and awareness raising.IP2's EOPO is water resources governance processes at the national and regional levels in the Greater Mekong Sub-region are more inclusive of civil society, women and marginalised social groups.

LONG_DESCRIPTION: The ANCP is a unique Australian aid program. It is a partnership between the Australian Government and accredited Australian NGOs. For over 40 years, this partnership has contributed to sustainable economic growth and poverty reduction in some of the world's poorest countries. The ANCP is the Australian Government's longest running and largest NGO program. The total value of the ANCP is $132.5 million in the 2019-20 financial year, of which Oxfam Australia will receive $10,125,709.00.

SHORT_DESCRIPTION: ENERGY TRANSITION MECHANISM IN VIET NAM
PROJECT_TITLE: Energy Transition Mechanism in Viet Nam
LONG_DESCRIPTION: The Asian Development Bank (ADB) led Energy Transition Mechanism (ETM) presents a solution to achieve the aspirational targets of South East Asian nations to mitigate climate change. The ETM is a new initiative in which blended finance is used to accelerate the retirement or repurposing of coal-fired power plants (CFPPs) to replace them with cleaner, more renewable sources of energy. ADB believes the ETM has the potential to be one of the biggest carbon reduction programmes in the world.
